task.name: Summarize open bugs
task.description: Summarize the open bugs in bugs.json and find the cause in the logs

mapCaption: Every call sends the whole history. One 40 KB file read stays in it for the rest of the task, and a failed JSON check sends the whole thing again.

issues.title: read_file puts a 40 KB export into context
issues.fixSummary: Return only the open bugs, or cap results at 1,500 characters.
issues.fix: The task needs the 29 open bugs, not all 200. Filter in the tool (status == open) or cap tool results at 1,500 characters with a note of the full size. The ~18,700-token result rides along in 7 of 8 calls; cut to ~375 tokens, that saves ~128,000 tokens per task.

code.snippet:
def read_file(path):
    """The whole bug export: ~40 KB of JSON."""

evidence.trace: huge-tool-result (3/3 runs): one ~18,726-token tool result, first in call 2 and carried in calls 2–8.

issues.diff:
- "content": RUN[b["name"]](b["input"])
+ out = RUN[b["name"]](b["input"])
+ "content": out if len(out) <= 1500 else out[:1500] + f"\n... (truncated, {len(out)} chars total)"

issues.title: Nothing is cached, and a timestamp would break caching anyway
issues.fixSummary: Remove the timestamp and mark the system prompt and history for caching.
issues.fix: 0 of 168,068 tokens were read from cache. ~134,700 tokens repeat a previous call's prefix and could be cache reads (billed at about a tenth of full price). The count shown is that 90% in full-price-equivalent tokens. Move the timestamp out of the system prompt (it changes on every run) and add cache_control to the system prompt and the last message.

code.snippet: SYSTEM = (f"You are a bug triage assistant. Current time: {datetime.now().isoformat()}. "

evidence.trace: no-cache (3/3 runs): cache_read = 0 and cache_write = 0 across 8 calls. unstable-prefix: the first call's system prompt differs between runs at the same size.

issues.diff:
- SYSTEM = (f"You are a bug triage assistant. Current time: {datetime.now().isoformat()}. "
+ SYSTEM = [{"type": "text", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"},
+            "text": "You are a bug triage assistant. ..."}]

issues.title: A non-JSON answer replays the whole conversation, three times
issues.fixSummary: Repair the answer with one small call instead of resending everything.
issues.fix: Calls 6–8 (80,227 tokens) exist only to get JSON. A small repair call ("Convert to JSON: <answer>") costs about 80 tokens. A second bug: body['messages'] is the same list the loop appends to, so each retry also resends the previous answer. Verify the repaired JSON keeps the same content.

evidence.trace: retry-storm (3/3 runs): calls 7 and 8 repeat call 6's request exactly; call 6 is call 5 plus its own answer.

issues.diff:
- answer = text_of(call_model(body))
+ answer = text_of(call_model({"model": "claude-haiku-5-5", "max_tokens": 300,
+     "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Convert to JSON: " + answer}]}))

issues.title: Old tool results stay in history at full size
issues.fixSummary: Shrink tool results to a short stub once the model has used them.
issues.fix: History grows from 0 to ~24,000 tokens over 8 calls and every turn is resent. Besides the big file (counted above), three 1,738-token search results are resent 12 times in total. Replace a tool result with a ~50-token stub after the next turn. Check that later answers don't need the trimmed details.

evidence.trace: history-growth (3/3 runs): 109,824 tokens of earlier turns sent again (overlaps with the 40 KB result).

issues.title: search_logs runs three times with the same query
issues.fixSummary: Answer repeat calls with "same result as above" instead of re-running them.
issues.fix: The model asked for search_logs("timeout") in calls 2, 3, and 4. Each repeat adds another 1,738-token copy that is resent in every later call. Deduplicate by (tool, arguments) and return a one-line note; also add a turn limit so a model that keeps repeating cannot run forever.

evidence.trace: repeated-tool-call (3/3 runs): 2 repeats of search_logs with identical arguments (calls 3, 4).

issues.title: The prompt asks for detail and allows 8,000 output tokens
issues.fixSummary: Ask for a brief answer and lower max_tokens to 500.
issues.fix: Each final answer is ~1,240 tokens for a task that needs a few sentences. The cost here is small because output is only 3% of the total, but long answers also grow history. Change "Explain in detail" to "Be brief" and set max_tokens to 500. Confirm the shorter answer still covers what users need.

code.snippet: "Summarize the open bugs and their likely cause. Explain in detail. Reply in JSON."

evidence.trace: verbose-output (3/3 runs): median final answer 1,238 tokens; max_tokens 8,000.

afterFix.label: measured
afterFix.note: Measured, not projected: clean_agent.py applies all six fixes and was run 3 times through the same proxy (2,103 tokens per task, 20% read from cache).

method.tokenizer: Usage from API responses (exact). Block sizes are chars/4 estimates scaled to the measured input of each call.
notes: Predicted (41,085) assumes the code's best case: one search, no retries. The gap to actual comes from the model repeating the search and the retry loop.
Ideal is the fixed agent (clean_agent.py), measured the same way.
Waste figures overlap: the 40 KB result is also part of resent history. They are not added up anywhere.
notMeasured: Dollar cost: this example runs against a fake API, so no prices apply.
Run-to-run variance: the fake model is deterministic, so all 3 runs match exactly. A real model will vary.
